source.title: Towards Understanding the Condensation of Neural Networks at Initial Training
source.authors: Hanxu Zhou; Qixuan Zhou; Tao Luo; Yaoyu Zhang; Z. Xu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and checklist.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures initial weight condensation and compares test accuracy across initialization methods, but does not test the claim versions about memorization, width, architecture, optimizers, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper’s condensation results and theoretical analysis do not measure training-versus-test error. Appendix A.4 compares test accuracy across initialization methods; those results are recorded as findings outside the listed versions. Cited prior work is not recorded as this study’s result.
record.test_reason: The study measures early weight condensation and compares initialization methods. Neither result tests V1–V8. Its proposed connection between condensation and generalization does not establish any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify activation multiplicity as a key determinant of early condensation and output complexity, argue that condensation initially reduces effective capacity, and propose subsequent capacity growth as a possible explanation of generalization. They do not demonstrate that this mechanism explains any of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates small-initialization condensation and its dependence on activation multiplicity; it does not implement the original sources’ memorization/generalization or intervention methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation function multiplicity and training data complexity affect the number of observed condensed orientations; the authors state that training data does not affect the maximal number.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.4 reports similar CIFAR-10 test accuracy across common and condensed FC-layer initializations: 86.73–88.07% for common methods and 86.88–88.26% for condensed methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With the tested ResNet18-like architecture, tanh FC layers, and Adam recipe, condensed initialization achieves test accuracy comparable to common initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Experiments link activation multiplicity p to a maximum of 2p initial condensed orientations; theory covers multiplicity one with arbitrary input dimension and one-dimensional input with arbitrary multiplicity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under small initialization, activation multiplicity constrains early weight condensation and effective network complexity.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems; text also includes 2022 proceedings header)
record.problems: No error bars or repeated-seed uncertainty are reported, as stated in the checklist. The generalization discussion is not directly evaluated beyond the test-accuracy comparison across initialization methods.

untested.parts: Matched random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with alternative measures.
Retraining after removal of memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct relation from tests to discusses; T6 is appropriate. All table comparisons concern FC-layer initialization; the convolutional component retains Glorot-normal initialization. The 18 accuracy entries can remain as outside-version findings, but should not serve as claim-test rows. Three trials are tabulated, although no error bars or formal equivalence analysis are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same training recipes.
Width sweep past interpolation and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Batch-size effects on generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training-test gap.
Effects of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.
